clue.text: Stiff material to resist something battering

parts.note: to buck is to resist or kick against something
a ram, as in battering ram, is used to batter down doors

explanation.surface: Advice on choosing a tough fabric that can withstand a pounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a coarse cloth stiffened with glue, used in bookbinding and to give shape to hats and collars.

clue.text: Paper initially backing up main files

indicators.note: the opening letters of the four following words are taken

explanation.surface: Advice on paperwork for backing up important computer files.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork or documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is informal British slang for unwanted paperwork, forms and documents.

clue.text: London, for example, wins one away from Uber — it reduces profits

parts.note: London is a capital city
to gain is to win

indicators.note: the one is taken away from the word for an Uber ride

parts.note: an Uber is a taxi summoned by app
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: London beats a ride-hailing company in a business story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' tells you to remove I (one) from TAXI, leaving TAX.
explanation.definitionFit: This levy is charged on the gain when an asset is sold, so it cuts what the seller makes.

clue.text: Man is rugby forward

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
pert and forward both mean cheeky or bold

explanation.surface: A man is said to play forward in rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests a rugby position, but here it means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is a man's first name, so it fits the crossword sense of a man.

clue.text: Sullen, introducing new poem of lament

indicators.note: the word for sullen has a letter introduced into it

parts.note: moody means sullen

explanation.surface: A gloomy poet introduces a new elegy.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is an ode sung by one voice, especially one mourning someone's death.

clue.text: In Panama, say, a little place where I live

indicators.note: the words a little are put in the middle of the Panama hat

parts.note: a Panama is an example of a hat
a bit means a little

explanation.surface: Someone describes their small home in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country where someone lives, but it is the straw hat; 'say' shows it is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or environment of an animal or plant, the place it lives.

clue.text: Say in what way it's a gun

indicators.note: say tells you the spoken phrase gives the answer

parts.note: in what way means how, so the phrase is how it's a

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to explain how something counts as a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short artillery piece that fires shells high into the air.

clue.text: Cabbage badger doesn't finish; firm, large one

indicators.note: the badger word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: brock is an old name for a badger
Co is short for company, a firm
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A badger fails to finish its greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli belongs to the cabbage family, Brassica oleracea.

clue.text: Be brave, like an unfortunate boxer?

definitions.meaning: to accept a setback without complaint
a boxer who is unlucky literally receives a punch to the jaw

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to endure hardship stoically; literally it is what a beaten fighter suffers to the jaw.

clue.text: Got roped in to play, explosively ruining it?

indicators.note: the words are put into play, juggled around

explanation.surface: Someone reluctantly recruited into a game wrecks it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: attacking a ship with a missile wrecks it with an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo something is to ruin it, literally by firing an explosive underwater missile.

clue.text: Dispose of bushy hair — revolting!

parts.note: a mop is a thick, untidy mass of hair
people who are up in arms or have risen up are revolting

explanation.surface: An instruction to get rid of a disgusting shaggy hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, but here it means rising in revolt, which is UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to deal with and finish off what remains, such as leftover enemy troops or spilt liquid.

clue.text: Queens' man's worry — knee being wrenched

indicators.note: the letters are twisted out of shape like a wrenched joint

explanation.surface: A man from Queens frets about his twisted knee.
explanation.walkthrough: Queens is a borough of New York City, so its residents are New Yorkers; the 's of man's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens is one of the five boroughs of New York City, so anyone living there is a native of that city.

clue.text: A stock Guardian figure?

parts.note: a person who guards a shop's stock, not a typical character from this newspaper

explanation.surface: A question about a stereotypical figure from the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock Guardian figure' suggests a cliché Guardian reader; read instead as one who guards the stock in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A store detective is employed by a shop to watch for shoplifters and protect its merchandise.

clue.text: Magistrates and newspapers in strenuous exercise

parts.note: the bench is a collective name for magistrates in court
the press means newspapers

explanation.surface: Court officials and reporters are caught up in a demanding workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench press is a weightlifting exercise in which a barbell is pushed up while lying on a bench.

clue.text: Feel sick, having eaten fish

indicators.note: the words Feel sick are said to have swallowed the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: Someone feels unwell after a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish, a traditional London food when jellied.

clue.text: Rich supply of water awaiting attention

parts.note: a well is a source of water dug into the ground
a job still to do is awaiting attention

explanation.surface: A plentiful water source that needs maintenance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like it describes the supply of water, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-to-do means being prosperous and comfortably off.

clue.text: In brief, fine state of musical theatre

definitions.text: In brief, fine state of musical theatre

parts.words: In brief, fine state of musical theatre
parts.note: a US state whose short form is the word for fine, and also a famous Rodgers and Hammerstein musical

explanation.surface: A short review praising the condition of musical theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The state's postal abbreviation is OK, which also means fine.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state is abbreviated OK and gave its name to a 1943 Broadway musical.

clue.text: Carelessly treading slope

indicators.note: the letters are put down without care, out of order

explanation.surface: A warning about walking on a slope without care.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the degree of incline of a road or hill.

clue.text: Solvers are excellent people

definitions.meaning: those who crack codes or puzzles
a cracker is British slang for an excellent person or thing

explanation.surface: A compliment to the people solving the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: One who cracks a problem solves it, and in British slang a cracker is something first-rate.

clue.text: Mark returns to school

indicators.note: the word for mark goes back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: a note is a mark or written comment

explanation.surface: A grade being given back at school.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English private school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known English boarding school.

clue.text: Somewhere to sleep with a girl

parts.note: a berth is a bunk on a ship or train

explanation.surface: A suggestive line about finding a bed with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a girl's name, fitting the crossword sense of a girl.

clue.text: Notice academics make extra charges

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
dons are university teachers

explanation.surface: A notice says lecturers are adding fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Add-ons are extras that cost more on top of a basic price.

clue.text: Sensational items for dressmaker

definitions.meaning: describing a prickling sensation, as when a limb wakes from numbness
the sharp tools a seamstress uses for pinning and sewing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a tingling feeling in the skin and the sewing kit a dressmaker relies on.

clue.text: Liberal toff re-elected, with many abstentions

indicators.note: most letters of the phrase abstain, leaving only a few inside

explanation.surface: An upper-class politician is re-elected on a low turnout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' suggests the political party, but it means generous or unrestricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Free and liberal both mean generous or unrestrained.

clue.text: Old dog in races is not inhibited

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: the dog's name is set inside the races

parts.note: TT stands for the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A former greyhound racing is described as uninhibited.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is an outgoing, sociable person, the opposite of shy and reserved.

clue.text: Unmarried parent is not the same

indicators.note: un- takes away M, the standard abbreviation for married

parts.note: a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A single parent is said to be different from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unmarried parent' suggests a single mother, but 'Unmarried' means remove the M (married) from the parent word.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means different or distinct from the one already mentioned.

clue.text: It beat time, a guide when one's at sea

definitions.text: a guide when one's at sea

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal or sex
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Something kept time as a navigational aid on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's at sea' doubles as being confused and being on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextant measures angles between stars and the horizon, letting sailors fix their position.

clue.text: Can bees suffer want?

indicators.note: the letters are made to suffer, being knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about whether bees can be in need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' looks like a verb, but here it is the noun for lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack or deficiency, the state of something being missing.
